description: A security engineering manager must finalize the response classification and remediation plan for a suspicious build-system credential exposure, incorporating input from platform engineering, compliance, and customer operations.

shared_context.S1: A deployment credential was exposed in a CI build log during yesterday's release.
shared_context.S2: The credential has been disabled, and the initial review found no confirmed unauthorized production changes.
shared_context.S3: The incident review is scheduled to close today at 4 PM.
shared_context.S4: The affected CI system is used for production deployments and stores build logs and deployment audit records in separate systems.

PF1.text: While tracing the CI job this morning, Mateo confirmed that the exposed credential was used by two production deployment jobs before it was disabled. He found this in the deployment audit records while working on a separate rollback issue and has not yet attached the records to the incident.

PF2.text: The current audit-control policy requires security-incident evidence for deployment credentials to be stored immutably for exactly 400 days. Hana confirmed the control wording during a routine quarterly audit this afternoon but has not updated the incident checklist.

PF3.text: Customer operations confirmed that exactly three regulated customers had deployment jobs using this credential, and their agreements require notice within 24 hours when a deployment credential accesses their environments. Leah found the account-specific clauses while preparing the weekly customer report and has not posted the list in the incident channel.

acceptance_conditions: The incident must be classified as SEV-1.
The deployment credential must be rotated.
Incident evidence must be retained immutably for exactly 400 days.
The plan must identify exactly three regulated customers for notification.
A 24-hour regulated-customer notification commitment must be recorded.
The production-use evidence must be cited as justification for the incident classification or credential rotation.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'regulated_customer_notification' and c['detail'] == 'within 24 hours' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The initial review shows no confirmed production impact, but confirmation that the credential was used by exactly two production deployment jobs changes the classification to SEV-1 and requires credential rotation.
The audit-control wording changes evidence retention from an unspecified ordinary period to exactly 400 immutable days.
The account review changes customer handling from no known notification obligation to notifying exactly three regulated customers within 24 hours.
